question: Tell me how you track down a bug that only happens sometimes, or that appeared recently.

scenes.sub: Don't guess. Reproduce, shrink, then narrow it down by halves.
scenes.say: Hunting a subtle bug. This question tests your method, not your luck. A calm, repeatable process beats staring at code and guessing.

scenes.head: Analogy: a detective, not a gambler
scenes.say: A detective does not accuse at random. First, reproduce: make the bug fail on demand, every time. Second, minimize: shrink the failing input until almost nothing is left. Third, bisect: halve the search space again and again. Fourth, fix it, and add a test to lock it in.

scenes.head: Minimize: halve the input until it is tiny

panels.code:
rows = load("big.csv")   # 10000 rows: fails
rows = rows[:5000]     # still fails
rows = rows[:40]       # still fails
rows = rows[:3]        # passes
rows = rows[:4]        # fails!
# row 4 is the culprit

scenes.say: Say a job fails on a file with ten thousand rows. Keep cutting. Half still fails. Forty rows still fails. Three rows pass, four rows fail. So row four is the culprit. Now you have a tiny repro that you can debug in minutes, and later turn into a regression test.

scenes.head: Bisect: eight commits, only three tests

changes.text: Test c5: bad, so c5 broke it

scenes.say: Now the bug appeared recently. Eight commits ago it worked, now it is broken. Test the middle commit. It passes, so the bug is later. Next test c6. It fails, so the bug is c5 or c6. In the last step, test c5. It fails, so c5 introduced the bug. Three tests for eight commits. A thousand commits need only ten.

scenes.head: Let git do the halving

panels.code:
git bisect start
git bisect bad            # HEAD is broken
git bisect good v1.2      # this tag worked
# git checks out the middle commit
./test.sh
git bisect good           # or: git bisect bad

# or fully automatic:
git bisect run ./test.sh
git bisect reset

scenes.say: In git, start a bisect, mark the current commit bad, and mark an old tag good. Git checks out the middle commit. You run your test, then say good or bad, and git jumps again. Or use bisect run with a script that exits zero for good, and git finds the commit alone. Reset when you are done.

scenes.head: In the interview
rows: Add logging, capture the real input
A good commit and an automatic test
scenes.say: Likely follow-ups. You can't reproduce it? Add logging and capture the real input. What does bisect need? A known good commit and an automatic test. Bug is not a commit? Check config, data and dependencies. After the fix, add a regression test. The mistake is changing code before you can reproduce the bug.

lines: First I reproduce the bug on demand, then shrink the input.
If it is a regression, I git bisect to find the first bad commit.
Then I fix it and add a regression test.
